tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

# Explainable AI: semester projects

## How this works

Read the card, then write a one-page plan: the question, the first experiment, and the result that would end the project early. Write that refuting result down before you run anything at scale. Then build the pipeline on a small slice, run the full experiment, and write it up.

Every project ends with a paper-like document (four to eight pages in a conference template) and a repository that reproduces every number in it. You can use coding agents. You must keep the prompts and the agent sessions that produced code in the repository, read every paper you cite, and produce every number in the paper from a file you made. The team's own listening is a check you run often. None of the projects needs a human study.

Each card gives the question, what is known, the terms, the first steps, the plan, what you deliver, the refuting result, where the paper could go, what you need, and what to watch out for. All five run on one workstation GPU. Two cards name a text variant if your team prefers detectors of machine-generated text. If you get stuck or the plan stops making sense, say so early. Please avoid finding out a day before returning the project that the ground truth was wrong.

## Projects

kind
attribution
audit
benchmark
measurement
verification

open all

5 of 5 projects

## X2

### Explanations of what no one can hear: how much of an audio model's decision, and of its explanation, lies below the masking threshold

Every bin of a spectrogram is either audible or masked by louder neighbours, and the masking threshold from psychoacoustics (the model inside MP3) says which. Deleting all energy below the threshold is a change no listener can hear. You will build the threshold, delete the sub-threshold energy, and measure per model how much of the decision and how much of the attribution mass disappears, across five tasks and three architectures. Then you will test whether that number predicts a model's accuracy drop under codecs, which discard the same energy first, and audit listenable explanations for the share of their audio that nobody can hear.

measurement
course form: own experiment, with a new metric and a software package
compute: one workstation GPU

#### The question

How much of what audio models compute rests on inaudible energy, how much of their explanations points at it, and does inaudible reliance predict a model's robustness to codecs?

#### What is known

Psychoacoustic attacks on speech recognition (2018, 2019) hide perturbations under the masking threshold and succeed, which shows that models respond to energy listeners cannot hear. A 2026 causal analysis finds that a practically inaudible change to one frequency flips an audio classifier's decision in over half the cases. Codec robustness of deepfake detectors (2025) and of provenance attribution (2026) was measured without its cause. Listenable explanations (2022, 2024) return audio the user is meant to hear, with no check that it is audible. A 2026 preprint moves the attribution maps of deepfake detectors with inaudible perturbations. Nobody has measured inaudible reliance as a property of models and of explanations, or linked it to codec robustness.

#### Terms used

masking threshold
: the level, per time-frequency bin, below which a listener cannot hear energy because louder neighbouring sound masks it. Computed by a psychoacoustic model from the signal itself.

sub-threshold deletion
: removing every bin below the threshold and resynthesizing the waveform. By construction the listener hears no change.

inaudible reliance
: the change in a model's output under sub-threshold deletion, and the share of an attribution map's mass in sub-threshold bins.

#### First steps

- Implement the masking threshold (the MPEG psychoacoustic model, or an open implementation you have checked) and confirm on ten clips, by listening, that the sub-threshold deletion is inaudible to the team.
- Run one classifier on 100 clips before and after the deletion and report the output change against the change between two different clips.
- Write down the refuting result.

#### Plan

- Set up five tasks with public models and data: speech recognition (Whisper), speaker verification, sound tagging (the Audio Spectrogram Transformer, PANNs), bird sound classification (BirdNET), and deepfake detection (AASIST, a SONICS detector). Use three architectures where the task has them and 300 clips per task.
- Measure the decision change under sub-threshold deletion per model and task, with the between-clip control and bootstrap intervals, at two stated playback levels and with two masking models.
- Measure the inaudible mass of four attribution methods (Integrated Gradients, Grad-CAM, LRP, occlusion) on the common grid, with a random-map control.
- Measure each model's accuracy drop under MP3 and Opus at three bitrates and test whether inaudible reliance predicts it across models.
- Audit listenable maps: the share of a listenable explanation's energy below the threshold of the mix it is played in. Build an audible-by-construction variant (masks restricted to audible bins) and report its faithfulness cost.
- Release the threshold code, the deletion, the metric and the tables as a package.

#### What you deliver

You deliver an inaudible-reliance number for about fifteen model-and-task pairs and an inaudible-mass number for every explainer on them, the codec-prediction table, the audibility audit of listenable maps with the audible variant, and a package that computes the metric on any model. If the numbers are near zero everywhere, you have shown that these models hear what listeners hear, and the metric becomes a certificate worth reporting.

#### What would refute it

The decision change and the attribution mass below threshold stay within the between-clip control for every model and task, at both playback levels and under both masking models.

#### Where the paper could go

Interspeech. ICASSP. WASPAA. A machine learning venue if the codec prediction holds.

#### What you need

Whisper, a speaker verifier, the Audio Spectrogram Transformer, PANNs, BirdNET, AASIST, a SONICS detector. LibriSpeech, a VoxCeleb test set, ESC-50 or an AudioSet evaluation subset, a bird sound set, ASVspoof 2019, SONICS. An MP3 and Opus encoder. Captum, Zennit. The listenable-maps code. One GPU, inference only.

#### Compute

one workstation GPU

#### Watch out for

A masking model is an approximation and depends on the playback level. State the level, use two masking models and report both. Resynthesis after deletion can add artifacts of its own. Check the deletion by ear on a sample of every task and keep the phase. The bird sound set's licence must allow research use.

#### Read first

- Adversarial Attacks Against Automatic Speech Recognition Systems via Psychoacoustic Hiding ([arXiv:1808.05665](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05665))
- Imperceptible, Robust, and Targeted Adversarial Examples for Automatic Speech Recognition ([arXiv:1903.10346](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.10346))
- I Guess That's Why They Call it the Blues: Causal Analysis for Audio Classifiers ([arXiv:2601.16675](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.16675))
- Measuring the Robustness of Audio Deepfake Detection under Real-World Corruptions ([arXiv:2503.17577](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.17577))
- Clean Accuracy Does Not Guarantee Provenance Robustness: A Prospective Codec-Stress Evaluation of Audio Attribution ([arXiv:2609.07981](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.07981))
- Listen to Interpret: Post-hoc Interpretability for Audio Networks with NMF ([arXiv:2202.11479](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.11479))
- Listenable Maps for Audio Classifiers ([arXiv:2403.13086](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.13086))
- Listenable Maps for Zero-Shot Audio Classifiers ([arXiv:2405.17615](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.17615))
- The Perceived Fragility of Explanations in Audio Models: Manipulation of Attribution with Unchanged Predictions ([arXiv:2606.14466](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.14466))
- A Framework for Evaluating Faithfulness in Explainable AI for Machine Anomalous Sound Detection ([arXiv:2601.19017](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.19017))

## Toolbox

You can use any tools you like. Say in the paper what you used. Good starting points: Captum and Zennit for attribution, Quantus for metrics, the audioLIME repository for LIME on audio. Compare maps on one common time-frequency grid so that numbers across models mean the same thing. Give every claim a control (a random map, or a random perturbation of the same size) and report bootstrap intervals over clips. Call a difference a difference only when the intervals say so.

Datasets you can start from: ASVspoof 2019 and 2021, In-the-Wild, PartialSpoof, SONICS, FakeMusicCaps, LibriSpeech, a VoxCeleb test set, ESC-50, a bird sound set, a public MIDI corpus. Models you can start from: AASIST, RawNet2, a wav2vec 2.0 detector, the SONICS detectors, the Audio Spectrogram Transformer, PANNs, Whisper, BirdNET, the listenable-maps code. Check every licence before you download.
=====
# 2026-11-05

## Done

- Made the environment with Poetry (Python 3.12, `.venv` in the project folder), `justfile` and pre-commit (ruff, mypy).
- Changed `AGENTS.md` and `KAGGLE.md` for this project: Poetry, `notes/`, `task_input/`, the Kaggle token in `.env`. Removed OpenSpec.
- Implemented the MPEG-1 psychoacoustic model 1 (`src/inaudible/masking.py`). The playback level is 96 dB SPL for a full-scale sine.
- Implemented the sub-threshold deletion with the phase kept (`src/inaudible/deletion.py`). STFT: Hann window, 512 points, 50 % overlap, at 44.1 kHz.
- Added an objective audibility check: the noise-to-mask ratio of the residual against the threshold of the original.
- Added the controls: resynthesis without a change, random deletion of the same number of bins, the between-clip control.
- Selected 100 ESC-50 clips (2 for each class, seed 0) and 10 clips for the listening test: `data/clips/esc50_t1.csv`.
- Added the tests: known signals for the threshold and the deletion, the measures, and the complete pipeline with a small model.
- Wrote the refuting result: `docs/refuting_result.md`.
- Job `ast-esc50-v1` on Kaggle: AST on the 100 clips (see `jobs/JOBS.md`). The job took 6 minutes on a T4: 4 minutes for the deletion on the CPU, 40 seconds for the model.
- Added the prototype notebook `notebooks/t1_prototype.ipynb`.

## First results (AST, ESC-50, 96 dB SPL, model 1)

Mean over 100 clips, with the 95 % bootstrap interval:

| Condition | Top-1 change | JS divergence |
|---|---|---|
| resynthesis | 0.00 | 0.000 |
| deletion | 0.33 [0.24, 0.42] | 0.139 [0.107, 0.174] |
| random_deletion | 0.92 [0.86, 0.97] | 0.635 [0.587, 0.681] |
| between_clips | 0.96 [0.92, 0.99] | 0.893 [0.863, 0.920] |

- The deletion removes 84 % of the bins and 16 % of the energy. The mean noise-to-mask ratio of the residual is -9.4 dB. The residual is above the threshold in 0.5 % of the bins.
- The deletion change is 16 % of the between-clip change. Thus this pair does not give the refuting result.
- Warning: in some clips, most of the deleted energy is below 100 Hz (rain: 73 %, sea waves: 64 %). The threshold in quiet is high there. Quiet clips (keyboard typing, peak -15 dBFS) lose much energy in the middle band. The listening test must check these clips first.

## Blockers

- The listening test is not done yet. The result is not valid before it.

## Plan

- The team listens to the 10 clips (original, deleted, residual, random) and writes the result into a note.
- Show the prototype in `notebooks/t1_prototype.ipynb`.
=====
# Research hypotheses and the refuting result

We wrote these hypotheses on 2026-11-05, before the first run at scale. We can change the decision rules only before the run of all models (T3).

## The question

Do audio models use sound that a human cannot hear? Do their explanations point at this sound?

## The hypotheses

**H1 (decisions).** Audio models use sound that a human cannot hear. If we remove only the inaudible part of a clip, the answer of the model changes.

**H2 (explanations).** Attribution maps put more weight on inaudible bins than a random map does.

**H3 (codecs).** MP3 and Opus also remove the inaudible part first. Thus a model that depends more on the inaudible part loses more accuracy under these codecs.

## The refuting result

The project is refuted if all these statements are true:

1. For every model and task, the removal of the inaudible part changes the answer of the model no more than a null change does (see below).
2. Statement 1 is true at both playback levels and under both masking models.
3. For every attribution method, the share of the map in inaudible bins is not larger than the share for a random map.

Then the models hear only what a human hears. The result is still useful: the metric becomes a certificate for a model.

## How we decide for one model and one task

A null change is a change that a human cannot hear and that removes no sound. Examples:

- a shift of the clip by a few samples
- a change of the level by 0.5 dB
- noise at -90 dBFS
- resynthesis without a change (STFT and inverse STFT)

The decision has three steps:

1. Measure the change of the model output under each null change. The noise floor of the model is the largest upper limit of the 95 % bootstrap intervals.
2. Measure the change under the removal of the inaudible part, with its 95 % bootstrap interval.
3. Compare the two values:
   - If the upper limit of the removal is below the noise floor, the removal has no effect (the refuting result for this pair).
   - If the lower limit of the removal is above the noise floor, the removal has an effect (H1 for this pair).
   - In all other cases, the result is not clear. Then we add clips.

The main measure is the Jensen-Shannon divergence between the outputs (see `src/inaudible/metrics.py`).

## The role of the between-clip change

The between-clip change is the change of the output between two different clips. We use it only as a scale. We give the effect of the removal as a percentage of the between-clip change. Then the numbers of different models have the same scale. The between-clip change is not a part of the decision.

    21	def synthesize(spec: np.ndarray, n_fft: int, length: int) -> np.ndarray:
    22	    """Inverse of analyze(), cut to the original length."""
    23	    _, x = istft(spec, window="hann", nperseg=n_fft, noverlap=n_fft // 2)
    24	    out = np.zeros(length)
    25	    out[: min(length, len(x))] = x[:length]
    26	    return out

    30	class Deletion:

     1	"""MPEG-1 psychoacoustic model 1 (ISO/IEC 11172-3, Annex D).
     2	
     3	The implementation follows the description in Painter and Spanias (2000), section V,
     4	and the reference code of toolame (psycho_1.c). It evaluates the threshold on every
     5	spectral line, not on the subsampled frequency grid of the standard.
     6	"""
     7	
     8	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
     9	
    10	import numpy as np
    11	
    12	# The one-sided power sum of a full-scale sine under a Hann window with "spectrum" scaling
    13	# (|sum(w x e)| / sum(w))^2 is 3/8 for every frequency. This value calibrates the dB SPL scale.
    14	_HANN_SINE_POWER = 3.0 / 8.0
    15	# The tonal neighbourhood of the standard is in lines of a 512-point FFT at 44.1 kHz.
    16	_REFERENCE_LINE_HZ = 44100.0 / 512.0
    17	
    18	
    19	def bark(freq_hz: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    20	    """Critical band rate (Zwicker) in Bark."""
    21	    f = np.asarray(freq_hz, dtype=float)
    22	    return 13.0 * np.arctan(0.00076 * f) + 3.5 * np.arctan((f / 7500.0) ** 2)
    23	
    24	
    25	def absolute_threshold(freq_hz: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    26	    """Threshold in quiet (Terhardt) in dB SPL. Frequencies below 20 Hz use the value at 20 Hz."""
    27	    f = np.maximum(np.asarray(freq_hz, dtype=float), 20.0) / 1000.0
    28	    return 3.64 * f**-0.8 - 6.5 * np.exp(-0.6 * (f - 3.3) ** 2) + 1e-3 * f**4
    29	
    30	
    31	def _spreading(dz: np.ndarray, power_db: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    32	    """Spreading function of model 1 in dB. dz is maskee minus masker in Bark."""
    33	    p = np.broadcast_to(power_db, dz.shape)
    34	    sf = np.full(dz.shape, -np.inf)
    35	    m = (dz >= -3) & (dz < -1)
    36	    sf[m] = 17 * dz[m] - 0.4 * p[m] + 11
    37	    m = (dz >= -1) & (dz < 0)
    38	    sf[m] = (0.4 * p[m] + 6) * dz[m]
    39	    m = (dz >= 0) & (dz < 1)
    40	    sf[m] = -17 * dz[m]
    41	    m = (dz >= 1) & (dz < 8)
    42	    sf[m] = (0.15 * p[m] - 17) * dz[m] - 0.15 * p[m]
    43	    return sf
    44	
    45	
    46	@dataclass
    47	class Model1:
    48	    """Masking threshold of MPEG-1 psychoacoustic model 1 for frames of one STFT.
    49	
    50	    playback_db is the SPL of a full-scale sine. The threshold depends on it through
    51	    the threshold in quiet and through the level-dependent spreading function.
    52	    """
    53	
    54	    sample_rate: int
    55	    n_fft: int = 512
    56	    playback_db: float = 96.0
    57	    freqs: np.ndarray = field(init=False, repr=False)
    58	    z: np.ndarray = field(init=False, repr=False)
    59	    quiet_db: np.ndarray = field(init=False, repr=False)
    60	    _band: np.ndarray = field(init=False, repr=False)
    61	    _neighbours: list[np.ndarray] = field(init=False, repr=False)
    62	
    63	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
    64	        self.freqs = np.arange(self.n_fft // 2 + 1) * self.sample_rate / self.n_fft
    65	        self.z = bark(self.freqs)
    66	        self.quiet_db = absolute_threshold(self.freqs)
    67	        self._band = np.floor(self.z).astype(int)
    68	        scale = _REFERENCE_LINE_HZ / (self.sample_rate / self.n_fft)
    69	        self._neighbours = []
    70	        for f in self.freqs:
    71	            ref = [2] if f < 5500 else [2, 3] if f < 11000 else [2, 3, 4, 5, 6]
    72	            self._neighbours.append(np.unique(np.maximum(2, np.round(np.array(ref) * scale).astype(int))))
    73	
    74	    def to_db(self, power: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    75	        """Convert a one-sided power spectrum ("spectrum" scaling, Hann window) to dB SPL."""
    76	        return self.playback_db + 10 * np.log10(np.maximum(power, 1e-30) / _HANN_SINE_POWER)
    77	
    78	    def maskers(self, x_db: np.ndarray) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    79	        """Find the tonal and noise maskers of one frame after decimation.
    80	
    81	        Returns the line index, the power in dB SPL and a flag (True for tonal) of each masker.
    82	        """
    83	        n = len(x_db)
    84	        tonal_idx: list[int] = []
    85	        for k in range(1, n - 1):
    86	            if not (x_db[k] > x_db[k - 1] and x_db[k] >= x_db[k + 1]):
    87	                continue
    88	            nb = self._neighbours[k]
    89	            nb = np.concatenate([k - nb, k + nb])
    90	            nb = nb[(nb >= 0) & (nb < n)]
    91	            if np.all(x_db[k] - x_db[nb] >= 7):
    92	                tonal_idx.append(k)
    93	        lin = 10 ** (x_db / 10)
    94	        tonal = np.array(tonal_idx, dtype=int)
    95	        tonal_db = np.array([10 * np.log10(lin[k - 1 : k + 2].sum()) for k in tonal])
    96	
    97	        # Noise maskers: the lines that are not near a tonal masker, summed in each critical band.
    98	        rest = lin.copy()
    99	        for k in tonal:
   100	            w = int(self._neighbours[k].max())
   101	            rest[max(0, k - w) : k + w + 1] = 0
   102	        noise_idx, noise_db = [], []
   103	        for b in np.unique(self._band):
   104	            lines = np.flatnonzero(self._band == b)
   105	            total = rest[lines].sum()
   106	            if total <= 0:
   107	                continue
   108	            centre = np.exp(np.mean(np.log(np.maximum(lines, 1))))
   109	            noise_idx.append(int(np.clip(np.round(centre), lines[0], lines[-1])))
   110	            noise_db.append(10 * np.log10(total))
   111	
   112	        idx = np.concatenate([tonal, np.array(noise_idx, dtype=int)])
   113	        power = np.concatenate([tonal_db, np.array(noise_db)])
   114	        is_tonal = np.concatenate([np.ones(len(tonal), bool), np.zeros(len(noise_idx), bool)])
   115	
   116	        # Decimation: remove maskers below the threshold in quiet, then the weaker one of two maskers within 0.5 Bark.
   117	        keep = power >= self.quiet_db[idx]
   118	        idx, power, is_tonal = idx[keep], power[keep], is_tonal[keep]
   119	        order = np.argsort(idx, kind="stable")

   126	                continue

   142	        idx, power, is_tonal = self.maskers(x_db)
   143	        total = 10 ** (self.quiet_db / 10)
   144	        if len(idx):

     6	def softmax(logits: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
     7	    z = logits - logits.max(axis=-1, keepdims=True)

    12	def js_divergence(a: np.ndarray, b: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    13	    """Jensen-Shannon divergence in bits between softmax(a) and softmax(b), row by row. Range [0, 1]."""
    14	    p, q = softmax(a), softmax(b)
    15	    m = (p + q) / 2
    16	
    17	    def kl(x: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    18	        return np.asarray(np.sum(x * (np.log2(np.maximum(x, 1e-30)) - np.log2(np.maximum(y, 1e-30))), axis=-1))
    19	
    20	    return np.clip((kl(p, m) + kl(q, m)) / 2, 0.0, 1.0)

    23	def confidence_drop(a: np.ndarray, b: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    24	    """Drop of the sigmoid probability of the top-1 class of a, from a to b, row by row. Range [-1, 1].
    25	
    26	    The models are multi-label, so each class has its own sigmoid probability.
    27	    """
    28	    k = a.argmax(axis=-1)
    29	    rows = np.arange(len(a))
    30	    return np.asarray(1 / (1 + np.exp(-a[rows, k])) - 1 / (1 + np.exp(-b[rows, k])))

    34	    """All measures of the change between two logit arrays of shape (clips, classes)."""
    35	    return {
    36	        "top1_changed": (a.argmax(axis=-1) != b.argmax(axis=-1)).astype(float),
    37	        "js_divergence": js_divergence(a, b),
    38	        "confidence_drop": confidence_drop(a, b),

    42	def between_clip_pairs(n: int, rng: np.random.Generator) -> np.ndarray:
    43	    """A partner for each clip, never the clip itself: the next clip in a random cyclic order."""
    44	    order = rng.permutation(n)
    45	    partner = np.empty(n, dtype=int)

    51	    values: np.ndarray, rng: np.random.Generator, n_boot: int = 10000, level: float = 0.95
    52	) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
    53	    """Mean and the percentile bootstrap interval of the mean, with resampling over clips."""

     1	"""Sub-threshold deletion: remove every STFT bin below the masking threshold and resynthesize.
     2	
     3	The deletion keeps the phase of the bins that stay. The same STFT gives the threshold,
     4	the mask and the resynthesis, so the mask and the threshold have the same grid.
     5	"""

     7	from dataclasses import dataclass
     8	
     9	import numpy as np
    10	from scipy.signal import istft, stft
    11	
    12	from inaudible.masking import Model1

    15	def analyze(x: np.ndarray, n_fft: int) -> np.ndarray:
    16	    """Complex STFT with a Hann window and 50 % overlap. Shape (lines, frames)."""
    17	    _, _, spec = stft(x, window="hann", nperseg=n_fft, noverlap=n_fft // 2)
    18	    return np.asarray(spec)
    19	
    20	
    21	def synthesize(spec: np.ndarray, n_fft: int, length: int) -> np.ndarray:
    22	    """Inverse of analyze(), cut to the original length."""
    23	    _, x = istft(spec, window="hann", nperseg=n_fft, noverlap=n_fft // 2)
    24	    out = np.zeros(length)
    25	    out[: min(length, len(x))] = x[:length]
    26	    return out
    27	
    28	
    29	@dataclass
    30	class Deletion:
    31	    """The result of a sub-threshold deletion of one clip."""
    32	
    33	    deleted: np.ndarray
    34	    audible: np.ndarray
    35	    spectrum_db: np.ndarray
    36	    threshold_db: np.ndarray
    37	
    38	    @property
    39	    def fraction_bins_deleted(self) -> float:
    40	        return float(1 - self.audible.mean())
    41	
    42	    @property
    43	    def fraction_energy_deleted(self) -> float:
    44	        power = 10 ** (self.spectrum_db / 10)
    45	        return float(power[~self.audible].sum() / power.sum())
    46	
    47	
    48	def delete_subthreshold(x: np.ndarray, model: Model1) -> Deletion:
    49	    """Remove all bins of x below the masking threshold of x."""
    50	    spec = analyze(x, model.n_fft)
    51	    x_db, thr = model.threshold(np.abs(spec) ** 2)
    52	    audible = x_db >= thr
    53	    deleted = synthesize(np.where(audible, spec, 0), model.n_fft, len(x))
    54	    return Deletion(deleted, audible, x_db, thr)
    55

    57	def resynthesize(x: np.ndarray, n_fft: int) -> np.ndarray:
    58	    """STFT and inverse STFT without a change. It shows the effect of the resynthesis alone."""
    59	    return synthesize(analyze(x, n_fft), n_fft, len(x))
    60

    62	def delete_random(x: np.ndarray, audible: np.ndarray, n_fft: int, rng: np.random.Generator) -> np.ndarray:
    63	    """Control: in each frame, remove the same number of bins as the deletion, at random lines."""
    64	    spec = analyze(x, n_fft)
    65	    keep = np.ones_like(audible)
    66	    n_lines = audible.shape[0]
    67	    for t, n_removed in enumerate((~audible).sum(axis=0)):
    68	        keep[rng.choice(n_lines, size=n_removed, replace=False), t] = False
    69	    return synthesize(np.where(keep, spec, 0), n_fft, len(x))

    72	def noise_to_mask(
    73	    original: np.ndarray, processed: np.ndarray, threshold_db: np.ndarray, model: Model1
    74	) -> dict[str, float]:
    75	    """Objective audibility check of a change, against the masking threshold of the original.
    76	
    77	    The residual (original minus processed) is inaudible in a bin if its power is below the threshold.
    78	    Returns the mean noise-to-mask ratio in dB and the fraction of bins with an audible residual.
    79	    """
    80	    residual = analyze(original - processed, model.n_fft)
    81	    thr = threshold_db
    82	    res_db = model.to_db(np.abs(residual) ** 2)
    83	    nmr = 10 ** ((res_db - thr) / 10)
    84	    return {

    86	        "fraction_bins_audible": float((res_db > thr).mean()),
    87	    }

     1	"""MPEG-1 psychoacoustic model 1 (ISO/IEC 11172-3, Annex D).
     2	
     3	The implementation follows the description in Painter and Spanias (2000), section V,
     4	and the reference code of toolame (psycho_1.c). It evaluates the threshold on every
     5	spectral line, not on the subsampled frequency grid of the standard.
     6	"""
     7	
     8	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
     9	
    10	import numpy as np
    11	
    12	# The one-sided power sum of a full-scale sine under a Hann window with "spectrum" scaling
    13	# (|sum(w x e)| / sum(w))^2 is 3/8 for every frequency. This value calibrates the dB SPL scale.
    14	_HANN_SINE_POWER = 3.0 / 8.0
    15	# The tonal neighbourhood of the standard is in lines of a 512-point FFT at 44.1 kHz.
    16	_REFERENCE_LINE_HZ = 44100.0 / 512.0
    17	
    18	
    19	def bark(freq_hz: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    20	    """Critical band rate (Zwicker) in Bark."""
    21	    f = np.asarray(freq_hz, dtype=float)
    22	    return 13.0 * np.arctan(0.00076 * f) + 3.5 * np.arctan((f / 7500.0) ** 2)
    23	
    24	
    25	def absolute_threshold(freq_hz: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    26	    """Threshold in quiet (Terhardt) in dB SPL. Frequencies below 20 Hz use the value at 20 Hz."""
    27	    f = np.maximum(np.asarray(freq_hz, dtype=float), 20.0) / 1000.0
    28	    return 3.64 * f**-0.8 - 6.5 * np.exp(-0.6 * (f - 3.3) ** 2) + 1e-3 * f**4
    29	
    30	
    31	def _spreading(dz: np.ndarray, power_db: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    32	    """Spreading function of model 1 in dB. dz is maskee minus masker in Bark."""
    33	    p = np.broadcast_to(power_db, dz.shape)
    34	    sf = np.full(dz.shape, -np.inf)
    35	    m = (dz >= -3) & (dz < -1)
    36	    sf[m] = 17 * dz[m] - 0.4 * p[m] + 11
    37	    m = (dz >= -1) & (dz < 0)
    38	    sf[m] = (0.4 * p[m] + 6) * dz[m]
    39	    m = (dz >= 0) & (dz < 1)
    40	    sf[m] = -17 * dz[m]
    41	    m = (dz >= 1) & (dz < 8)
    42	    sf[m] = (0.15 * p[m] - 17) * dz[m] - 0.15 * p[m]
    43	    return sf
    44	
    45	
    46	@dataclass
    47	class Model1:
    48	    """Masking threshold of MPEG-1 psychoacoustic model 1 for frames of one STFT.
    49	
    50	    playback_db is the SPL of a full-scale sine. The threshold depends on it through
    51	    the threshold in quiet and through the level-dependent spreading function.
    52	    """
    53	
    54	    sample_rate: int
    55	    n_fft: int = 512
    56	    playback_db: float = 96.0
    57	    freqs: np.ndarray = field(init=False, repr=False)
    58	    z: np.ndarray = field(init=False, repr=False)
    59	    quiet_db: np.ndarray = field(init=False, repr=False)
    60	    _band: np.ndarray = field(init=False, repr=False)
    61	    _neighbours: list[np.ndarray] = field(init=False, repr=False)
    62	
    63	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
    64	        self.freqs = np.arange(self.n_fft // 2 + 1) * self.sample_rate / self.n_fft
    65	        self.z = bark(self.freqs)
    66	        self.quiet_db = absolute_threshold(self.freqs)
    67	        self._band = np.floor(self.z).astype(int)
    68	        scale = _REFERENCE_LINE_HZ / (self.sample_rate / self.n_fft)
    69	        self._neighbours = []
    70	        for f in self.freqs:
    71	            ref = [2] if f < 5500 else [2, 3] if f < 11000 else [2, 3, 4, 5, 6]
    72	            self._neighbours.append(np.unique(np.maximum(2, np.round(np.array(ref) * scale).astype(int))))
    73	
    74	    def to_db(self, power: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    75	        """Convert a one-sided power spectrum ("spectrum" scaling, Hann window) to dB SPL."""
    76	        return self.playback_db + 10 * np.log10(np.maximum(power, 1e-30) / _HANN_SINE_POWER)
    77	
    78	    def maskers(self, x_db: np.ndarray) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    79	        """Find the tonal and noise maskers of one frame after decimation.
    80	
    81	        Returns the line index, the power in dB SPL and a flag (True for tonal) of each masker.
    82	        """
    83	        n = len(x_db)
    84	        tonal_idx: list[int] = []
    85	        for k in range(1, n - 1):
    86	            if not (x_db[k] > x_db[k - 1] and x_db[k] >= x_db[k + 1]):
    87	                continue
    88	            nb = self._neighbours[k]
    89	            nb = np.concatenate([k - nb, k + nb])
    90	            nb = nb[(nb >= 0) & (nb < n)]
    91	            if np.all(x_db[k] - x_db[nb] >= 7):
    92	                tonal_idx.append(k)
    93	        lin = 10 ** (x_db / 10)
    94	        tonal = np.array(tonal_idx, dtype=int)
    95	        tonal_db = np.array([10 * np.log10(lin[k - 1 : k + 2].sum()) for k in tonal])
    96	
    97	        # Noise maskers: the lines that are not near a tonal masker, summed in each critical band.
    98	        rest = lin.copy()
    99	        for k in tonal:
   100	            w = int(self._neighbours[k].max())
   101	            rest[max(0, k - w) : k + w + 1] = 0
   102	        noise_idx, noise_db = [], []
   103	        for b in np.unique(self._band):
   104	            lines = np.flatnonzero(self._band == b)
   105	            total = rest[lines].sum()
   106	            if total <= 0:
   107	                continue
   108	            centre = np.exp(np.mean(np.log(np.maximum(lines, 1))))
   109	            noise_idx.append(int(np.clip(np.round(centre), lines[0], lines[-1])))
   110	            noise_db.append(10 * np.log10(total))

   112	        idx = np.concatenate([tonal, np.array(noise_idx, dtype=int)])
   113	        power = np.concatenate([tonal_db, np.array(noise_db)])
   114	        is_tonal = np.concatenate([np.ones(len(tonal), bool), np.zeros(len(noise_idx), bool)])

   116	        # Decimation: remove maskers below the threshold in quiet, then the weaker one of two maskers within 0.5 Bark.
   117	        keep = power >= self.quiet_db[idx]
   118	        idx, power, is_tonal = idx[keep], power[keep], is_tonal[keep]
   119	        order = np.argsort(idx, kind="stable")
   120	        idx, power, is_tonal = idx[order], power[order], is_tonal[order]
   121	        alive = np.ones(len(idx), bool)
   122	        i = 0
   123	        while i < len(idx):
   124	            if not alive[i]:
   125	                i += 1
   126	                continue
   127	            j = i + 1
   128	            while j < len(idx) and not alive[j]:
   129	                j += 1
   130	            if j < len(idx) and self.z[idx[j]] - self.z[idx[i]] < 0.5:
   131	                if power[j] > power[i]:
   132	                    alive[i] = False
   133	                    i = j
   134	                else:
   135	                    alive[j] = False
   136	                continue
   137	            i = j
   138	        return idx[alive], power[alive], is_tonal[alive]
   139	
   140	    def frame_threshold(self, x_db: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
   141	        """Global masking threshold in dB SPL for one frame, given its spectrum in dB SPL."""
   142	        idx, power, is_tonal = self.maskers(x_db)
   143	        total = 10 ** (self.quiet_db / 10)
   144	        if len(idx):
   145	            zj = self.z[idx][:, None]
   146	            pj = power[:, None]
   147	            dz = self.z[None, :] - zj
   148	            offset = np.where(is_tonal, -0.275 * self.z[idx] - 6.025, -0.175 * self.z[idx] - 2.025)[:, None]
   149	            individual = pj + offset + _spreading(dz, pj)
   150	            total = total + (10 ** (individual / 10)).sum(axis=0)
   151	        return np.asarray(10 * np.log10(total))
   152	
   153	    def threshold(self, power: np.ndarray) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
   154	        """Masking threshold for a power spectrogram of shape (lines, frames).
   155	
   156	        Returns the spectrogram and the threshold, both in dB SPL.
   157	        """
   158	        x_db = self.to_db(power)
   159	        thr = np.stack([self.frame_threshold(x_db[:, t]) for t in range(x_db.shape[1])], axis=1)

     1	"""Change of a model output, the between-clip control and bootstrap intervals."""
     2	
     3	import numpy as np
     4	
     5	
     6	def softmax(logits: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
     7	    z = logits - logits.max(axis=-1, keepdims=True)
     8	    e = np.exp(z)
     9	    return np.asarray(e / e.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True))
    10	
    11	
    12	def js_divergence(a: np.ndarray, b: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    13	    """Jensen-Shannon divergence in bits between softmax(a) and softmax(b), row by row. Range [0, 1]."""
    14	    p, q = softmax(a), softmax(b)
    15	    m = (p + q) / 2
    16	
    17	    def kl(x: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    18	        return np.asarray(np.sum(x * (np.log2(np.maximum(x, 1e-30)) - np.log2(np.maximum(y, 1e-30))), axis=-1))
    19	
    20	    return np.clip((kl(p, m) + kl(q, m)) / 2, 0.0, 1.0)
    21	
    22	
    23	def confidence_drop(a: np.ndarray, b: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    24	    """Drop of the sigmoid probability of the top-1 class of a, from a to b, row by row. Range [-1, 1].
    25	
    26	    The models are multi-label, so each class has its own sigmoid probability.
    27	    """
    28	    k = a.argmax(axis=-1)
    29	    rows = np.arange(len(a))
    30	    return np.asarray(1 / (1 + np.exp(-a[rows, k])) - 1 / (1 + np.exp(-b[rows, k])))
    31	
    32	
    33	def output_change(a: np.ndarray, b: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
    34	    """All measures of the change between two logit arrays of shape (clips, classes)."""
    35	    return {
    36	        "top1_changed": (a.argmax(axis=-1) != b.argmax(axis=-1)).astype(float),
    37	        "js_divergence": js_divergence(a, b),
    38	        "confidence_drop": confidence_drop(a, b),
    39	    }

    42	def between_clip_pairs(n: int, rng: np.random.Generator) -> np.ndarray:
    43	    """A partner for each clip, never the clip itself: the next clip in a random cyclic order."""
    44	    order = rng.permutation(n)
    45	    partner = np.empty(n, dtype=int)
    46	    partner[order] = np.roll(order, -1)
    47	    return partner
    48	
    49	
    50	def bootstrap_ci(
    51	    values: np.ndarray, rng: np.random.Generator, n_boot: int = 10000, level: float = 0.95
    52	) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
    53	    """Mean and the percentile bootstrap interval of the mean, with resampling over clips."""
    54	    values = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    55	    means = values[rng.integers(0, len(values), size=(n_boot, len(values)))].mean(axis=1)
    56	    lo, hi = np.quantile(means, [(1 - level) / 2, (1 + level) / 2])
    57	    return float(values.mean()), float(lo), float(hi)

--- a/docs/refuting_result.md
+++ b/docs/refuting_result.md
@@ -1,27 +1,49 @@
-# Refuting result
+# Research hypotheses and the refuting result
 
-We wrote this result down on 2026-11-05, before the first run at scale.
+We wrote these hypotheses on 2026-11-05, before the first run at scale. We can change the decision rules only before the run of all models (T3).
 
-## The statement of the project card
+## The question
 
-The decision change and the attribution mass below the threshold stay within the between-clip control for every model and task. This applies at both playback levels and under both masking models.
+Do audio models use sound that a human cannot hear? Do their explanations point at this sound?
 
-## The test for one model and one task
+## The hypotheses
 
-We use these conditions (see `src/inaudible/experiment.py`):
+**H1 (decisions).** Audio models use sound that a human cannot hear. If we remove only the inaudible part of a clip, the answer of the model changes.
 
-- `deletion`: the sub-threshold deletion.
-- `resynthesis`: STFT and inverse STFT without a change.
-- `random_deletion`: the same number of bins per frame, removed at random lines.
-- `between_clips`: the output of a different clip.
+**H2 (explanations).** Attribution maps put more weight on inaudible bins than a random map does.
 
-The main measure is the Jensen-Shannon divergence between the outputs. The other measures are the change of the top-1 class and the cosine distance of the logits. Each value has a 95 % bootstrap interval over the clips.
+**H3 (codecs).** MP3 and Opus also remove the inaudible part first. Thus a model that depends more on the inaudible part loses more accuracy under these codecs.
 
-The deletion has no measurable effect on a model if both conditions are true:
+## The refuting result
 
-1. The interval of `deletion` overlaps the interval of `resynthesis`.
-2. The upper limit of the interval of `deletion` is less than 5 % of the mean of `between_clips`.
+The project is refuted if all these statements are true:
 
-The project is refuted if this result occurs for every model and task, at both playback levels, under both masking models, and for the attribution mass.
+1. For every model and task, the removal of the inaudible part changes the answer of the model no more than a null change does (see below).
+2. Statement 1 is true at both playback levels and under both masking models.
+3. For every attribution method, the share of the map in inaudible bins is not larger than the share for a random map.
 
-The 5 % limit is a decision of the team. We can change it only before the run of all models (T3).
+Then the models hear only what a human hears. The result is still useful: the metric becomes a certificate for a model.
+
+## How we decide for one model and one task
+
+A null change is a change that a human cannot hear and that removes no sound. Examples:
+
+- a shift of the clip by a few samples
+- a change of the level by 0.5 dB
+- noise at -90 dBFS
+- resynthesis without a change (STFT and inverse STFT)
+
+The decision has three steps:
+
+1. Measure the change of the model output under each null change. The noise floor of the model is the largest upper limit of the 95 % bootstrap intervals.
+2. Measure the change under the removal of the inaudible part, with its 95 % bootstrap interval.
+3. Compare the two values:
+   - If the upper limit of the removal is below the noise floor, the removal has no effect (the refuting result for this pair).
+   - If the lower limit of the removal is above the noise floor, the removal has an effect (H1 for this pair).
+   - In all other cases, the result is not clear. Then we add clips.
+
+The main measure is the Jensen-Shannon divergence between the outputs (see `src/inaudible/metrics.py`).
+
+## The role of the between-clip change

=== cell 0 markdown
# T1 prototype: sub-threshold deletion on 100 ESC-50 clips

This notebook shows the results of the job `ast-esc50-v1` (see `jobs/JOBS.md`). All logic is in `src/inaudible/`.

The pipeline:

1. Compute the masking threshold of each clip (MPEG-1 psychoacoustic model 1, 96 dB SPL for a full-scale sine).
2. Remove every STFT bin below the threshold and resynthesize the waveform with the phase kept.
3. Give the original and the changed clips to AST and compare the outputs.

The controls: `resynthesis` (STFT and inverse STFT without a change), `random_deletion` (the same number of bins per frame at random lines) and `between_clips` (the output of a different clip). The refuting result is in `docs/refuting_result.md`.

To get the outputs, run `just fetch 2026-11-05_01_ast-esc50-v1`.
=== cell 1 code
import json
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import yaml
from IPython.display import Audio, Markdown, display

from inaudible.data import read_audio
from inaudible.deletion import analyze, delete_subthreshold
from inaudible.masking import Model1

ROOT = Path.cwd().parent if Path.cwd().name == "notebooks" else Path.cwd()
OUT = ROOT / "jobs/runs/2026-11-05_01_ast-esc50-v1/output/ast-esc50-v1"
cfg = yaml.safe_load((OUT / "config.yaml").read_text())
env = json.loads((OUT / "environment.json").read_text())
metrics = json.loads((OUT / "metrics.json").read_text())
summary = pd.read_csv(OUT / "summary.csv")
clips = pd.read_csv(OUT / "clips.csv")
print("commit", env["commit"], "| device", env["device"], "| model", env["model"])
print("versions", env["versions"])
print({k: round(v, 1) for k, v in metrics.items() if k.startswith("time")}, "| clips", metrics["n_clips"])
=== cell 2 markdown
## How much the deletion removes, and is the change inaudible?

- `fraction_bins_deleted`, `fraction_energy_deleted`: the share of STFT bins and of energy below the threshold.
- `nmr_db_*`: the mean noise-to-mask ratio of the residual (original minus changed clip) against the threshold of the original. A value below 0 dB means that the residual is under the threshold on average.
- `fraction_bins_audible_*`: the share of bins where the residual is above the threshold.
=== cell 3 code
def fmt(df):
    return df.assign(value=lambda d: [f"{m:.4g} [{lo:.4g}, {hi:.4g}]" for m, lo, hi in zip(d["mean"], d.ci_low, d.ci_high)])

display(fmt(summary[summary.condition == "audio"])[["measure", "value"]].set_index("measure"))
=== cell 4 markdown
## Change of the AST output

Each cell is the mean over the clips with the 95 % bootstrap interval. `top1_changed` is the share of clips with a different top-1 class.
=== cell 5 code
change = fmt(summary[summary.condition != "audio"])
order = ["resynthesis", "deletion", "random_deletion", "between_clips"]
display(change.pivot(index="condition", columns="measure", values="value").loc[order])
=== cell 6 code
measures = [m for m in ["js_divergence", "top1_changed", "confidence_drop", "cosine_distance"] if m in set(summary.measure)]
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(13, 3.2), sharey=True)
for ax, measure in zip(axes, measures):
    d = summary[(summary.measure == measure)].set_index("condition").loc[order]
    y = np.arange(len(order))
    ax.errorbar(d["mean"], y, xerr=[d["mean"] - d.ci_low, d.ci_high - d["mean"]], fmt="o", ms=8,
                color="#3b6ea8", ecolor="#3b6ea8", elinewidth=2, capsize=0)
    ax.set_title(measure, fontsize=11)
    ax.set_xscale("symlog", linthresh=1e-2)
    ax.grid(axis="x", color="#e3e3e3", linewidth=0.8)
    for side in ["top", "right"]:
        ax.spines[side].set_visible(False)
axes[0].set_yticks(y, order)
axes[0].invert_yaxis()
fig.suptitle("Change of the AST output against the original clip (mean, 95 % bootstrap interval)", fontsize=12)
fig.tight_layout()
=== cell 7 markdown
## The effect of the deletion on the scale of the between-clip change

The decision rule is in `docs/refuting_result.md`. It needs the noise floor of the model from the null changes. The job `ast-esc50-v1` does not have them yet. Here we show only the effect as a percentage of the between-clip change.
=== cell 8 code
js = summary[summary.measure == "js_divergence"].set_index("condition")
between = js.loc["between_clips", "mean"]
display(Markdown(
    f"Deletion: **{js.loc['deletion', 'mean'] / between:.1%}** of the between-clip change "
    f"(95 % interval {js.loc['deletion', 'ci_low'] / between:.1%} to {js.loc['deletion', 'ci_high'] / between:.1%})."
))
=== cell 9 markdown
## Clips with a different top-1 class after the deletion
=== cell 10 code
cols = ["filename", "category", "top1_original", "top1_deletion", "js_divergence_deletion", "fraction_energy_deleted"]
display(clips.loc[clips.top1_changed_deletion == 1, cols].sort_values("js_divergence_deletion", ascending=False))
=== cell 11 code
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.5, 4))
ax.scatter(clips.fraction_energy_deleted, clips.js_divergence_deletion, s=40, color="#3b6ea8",
           edgecolor="white", linewidth=1.5)
ax.set_xscale("log")
ax.set_xlabel("share of energy deleted")
ax.set_ylabel("JS divergence (deletion)")
ax.set_title("Each dot is one clip", fontsize=11)
ax.grid(color="#e3e3e3", linewidth=0.8)
for side in ["top", "right"]:
    ax.spines[side].set_visible(False)
fig.tight_layout()
=== cell 12 markdown
## The threshold and the deletion on one clip

The DSP part runs locally on the CPU. It uses the original clip from the listening set.
=== cell 13 code
listen = clips[clips.listen == 1].reset_index(drop=True)
name = listen.filename[0]
x, sr = read_audio(OUT / "listening" / name.replace(".wav", "_original.wav"))
model = Model1(sr, cfg["masking"]["n_fft"], cfg["masking"]["playback_db"])
res = delete_subthreshold(x, model)
t = np.arange(res.spectrum_db.shape[1]) * (model.n_fft // 2) / sr
kw = dict(origin="lower", aspect="auto", extent=[t[0], t[-1], 0, sr / 2000])
db = dict(cmap="Blues", vmin=0, vmax=100)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(14, 3.6), sharey=True)
im = axes[0].imshow(res.spectrum_db, **db, **kw)
axes[0].set_title("spectrum (dB SPL)")
fig.colorbar(im, ax=axes[0])
im = axes[1].imshow(res.threshold_db, **db, **kw)
axes[1].set_title("masking threshold (dB SPL)")
fig.colorbar(im, ax=axes[1])
axes[2].imshow(res.audible, cmap="Greys", **kw)
axes[2].set_title(f"audible bins (black): {1 - res.fraction_bins_deleted:.1%}")
axes[0].set_ylabel("frequency (kHz)")
for ax in axes:
    ax.set_xlabel("time (s)")
fig.suptitle(f"{name} ({listen.category[0]})", fontsize=12)
fig.tight_layout()
=== cell 14 code
frame = int(np.argmax(res.spectrum_db.max(axis=0)))
f = model.freqs / 1000
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 3.6))
ax.plot(f, res.spectrum_db[:, frame], color="#3b6ea8", lw=2, label="spectrum")
ax.plot(f, res.threshold_db[:, frame], color="#222222", lw=2, label="masking threshold")
ax.plot(f, model.quiet_db, color="#999999", lw=2, ls="--", label="threshold in quiet")
ax.set_ylim(-20, 110)
ax.set_xscale("log")
ax.set_xlabel("frequency (kHz)")
ax.set_ylabel("dB SPL")
ax.set_title(f"One frame at {t[frame]:.2f} s", fontsize=11)
ax.legend(frameon=False)
ax.grid(color="#e3e3e3", linewidth=0.8)
for side in ["top", "right"]:
    ax.spines[side].set_visible(False)
fig.tight_layout()
=== cell 15 markdown
## Listening test (10 clips)

For each clip: the original, the clip after the deletion, the deleted residual alone, and the random deletion control. The original and the deleted clip must sound the same. The random control must sound different. Play at a fixed, comfortable level. Write the result of each team member into a note.
=== cell 16 code
for row in listen.itertuples():
    stem = row.filename[:-4]
    display(Markdown(f"**{row.category}** `{row.filename}`: top-1 {row.top1_original} -> {row.top1_deletion}"))
    for kind in ["original", "deleted", "residual", "random"]:
        print(kind)
        display(Audio(str(OUT / "listening" / f"{stem}_{kind}.wav")))
